testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times while driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When you walk up to your vehicle before the pre-trip inspection, what should you look for that signals a problem?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: When you approach a vehicle for inspection, look underneath for oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaking onto the ground. Any leak shows a problem that must be fixed before you drive.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles need ____ to shift gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to shift gears. Release the gas, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Then release the clutch, let the engine speed match the gear, push in the clutch again, shift to the new gear, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: Water on bridges:

options.text: Usually freezes before water on other parts of the road.
Usually freezes after water on other parts of the road.
Is not a concern in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually freezes before water on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up
Prevent the air compressor from overheating
Prevent the front brakes from working on ice
Prevent brakes from being used if downshifting would work better

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: An anti-lock braking system (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery roads.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you before you reach the legal limit. One drink will bring a 200-pound person to a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent.

questions.question: Loading cargo:

options.text: Must be done by the driver.
Can be done by another person who is responsible for the cargo's safety.
Can be done by another person, but the driver is responsible for the cargo's safety.
Must be done by a shipping company employee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be done by another person, but the driver is responsible for the cargo's safety.
questions.explanation: No matter who loads the cargo, the driver is always responsible for making sure it is safe.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection part of the skills test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you will check and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show your knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you will check and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must explain to the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: A rim with one missing lug nut is acceptable if it has at least four other lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is acceptable if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is unsafe and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are acceptable for wheels on rear axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is unsafe and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lug nuts are dangerous. Bent or cracked lock rings are not safe. Wheels or rims with welded repairs are not safe.

questions.question: Once cargo is secured:

options.text: You can drive the entire trip without checking it.
You can drive for at least eight hours without checking it.
You should check it every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check it every three hours or 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive slowly and carefully near road workers.

questions.question: If driving a vehicle with a manual transmission, how can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward, partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake. Use the parking brake if needed to keep your vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Only time will lower your BAC as your body processes the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the truck is not overloaded.
Make sure the cargo is balanced.
Make sure the cargo is secured properly.
Place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place breakable items under heavier items.
questions.explanation: Drivers should check that cargo is properly secured, balanced, and not overloaded. Breakable items should not be placed under heavier items.

questions.question: What is the minimum size allowed for a hazard placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better fuel mileage.
It may be hard for you to see the road.
The tires may not support the weight.

questions.explanation: A high center of gravity increases the risk of your vehicle tipping over. This happens when cargo is piled high or heavy cargo is placed on top of a load.

questions.question: When going down a long downgrade, how should you brake?

options.text: Mostly use the brakes and downshift occasionally.
Downshift first, then use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use your engine's braking power to control your speed. Use your brakes only for extra slowing or stopping if needed.

questions.question: What can happen if a parking brake is used in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: In very wet, freezing weather, parking brakes can freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, you should:

options.text: Not worry because another vehicle will likely hit it first.
Swerve into another lane of traffic.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see objects in your lane. Even a cardboard box could contain heavy or hard items that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. On equipped vehicles, the lever is on the dashboard.

questions.question: If a driver operates in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license type should they choose?
questions.explanation: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must choose a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what is the safest thing to do?
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road, other vehicles, and hazards. Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: If a vehicle's ABS stops working while driving, what should the driver do?

options.text: Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If the ABS is not working, the vehicle's basic braking still works. Drive and brake normally as usual.

questions.question: What task might be included in a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When must a written vehicle inspection report be signed?

options.text: Only if defects were found and confirmed to be repaired.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and confirmed to be repaired.
questions.explanation: You must sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and confirmed to be repaired or determined to not need repair.

questions.question: If wheel bearing seals are leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Add more grease until the seal is full.
Add brake fluid to the bearing.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, wheel bearing seals should not leak. If you find anything unsafe, get it fixed. Federal and state laws prohibit driving an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving dangerous?

options.text: It causes both mental and physical distraction.
A message may upset the driver.
Texts may be more interesting than driving.
It is less efficient than a phone call.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes both mental and physical distraction.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts you both mentally and physically.

questions.question: On a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads. It is harder to stop or turn on slippery surfaces, so adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: How much water is needed on a road for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A large amount, like a big puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when vehicle tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. It does not require much water to happen.

questions.question: How many licenses can a driver have?

options.text: Two licenses, one for cars and one for trucks.
One license for each state where they plan to drive.
A regular license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: A person cannot have more than one license. States use a computer database to share driver information and prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, what should a driver do?

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads need special permits. They may only be allowed on the road at certain times of day.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Taking trips during hours when you would normally be asleep

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking trips during hours when you would normally be asleep
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get a full night's sleep before driving, have someone share driving duties, drive during your normal waking hours, and avoid medications that make you drowsy.

questions.question: What is a danger when a large truck swerves to avoid a hazard?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.
Other vehicles may do the same thing.

questions.explanation: Swerving is sometimes safer than stopping. However, swerving a top-heavy vehicle or one pulling trailers can cause it to roll over.

questions.question: When driving below 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, keep one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a crash, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. You need a firm grip to turn quickly.

questions.question: What is the lowest blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at which it is illegal to operate a CMV?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. If convicted, you will lose your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, engage the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: What is the minimum license suspension period if you refuse a blood alcohol test?
questions.explanation: Refusing a blood alcohol test is a serious violation. A first offense results in loss of your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, what happens?

options.text: The low pressure warning light turns on.
The low pressure warning light turns off.

questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They allow rainwater to enter air tanks.
They remove water and oil from air tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the system. If these build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system has very low pressure, what happens?

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system has very low pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop your vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check for: cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: When parked on the side of a road, you should:

options.text: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What color are ABS warning lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lamps.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A large amount, like a big puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You don't need a lot of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: When you must stop on a highway, how far behind your vehicle should warning devices be placed?
questions.explanation: When stopping your vehicle on a highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.explanation: More than 10 degrees of steering wheel play (about two inches on a 20-inch wheel) makes steering difficult.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method?

options.text: Apply brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
Apply brakes halfway and keep wheels rolling.
Apply brakes fully until wheels lock and vehicle stops.
Apply the emergency brake until the vehicle slows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking for emergency stops means: apply brakes fully until they lock, release brakes until wheels roll, then repeat this process.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert?

options.text: Don't wear sunglasses during the day.
Have another person ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have another person ride with you.
questions.explanation: To stay alert while driving, wear sunglasses to reduce eye strain, keep the cab cool, avoid heavy foods, and travel with someone who can help with driving duties.
